what: Playwright WebKit on Windows boot probes, one shared process per run (a new context per load, as the suites do), ready within 45 s; base = c2b9409 (exported tree), work = G2 working tree
reading: Every 4th load of a process loses its WebGL context (loads 3, 7, 11 of 0-based), for the base and the G2 tree alike when each runs alone; whether the page recovers within 45 s varies (base 1 of 3 recovered, work 0 of 3). In the interleaved runs the losing positions fell on work loads (ABBA 5/5, BAAB 3 failures + 1 recovered, base 1 recovered), which the alone runs do not support as a tree effect. Every first-attempt failure in the WebKit suites was a ready timeout or "WebGL: context lost." and passed on retry (U21). Not caused by G2 as far as these probes show; samples are small.
